title: ProjectE power-up sequencing and per-rail noise budget
description: Output of tools/scripts/board/rail_budget.py. Both halves concern a property no ERC and no DRC can reach: a netlist proves an enable pin is CONNECTED, never that the rail attached to it can turn the regulator on, because that needs a datasheet threshold and a rail voltage and a netlist carries neither. A board can be ERC-clean, DRC-clean, and still have a regulator whose enable clears its own V_EN(HI) at room temperature and misses it at the cold corner.

en_threshold_v.description: Datasheet V_EN(HI). null means it was not declared, which is reported as NO_COVERAGE rather than filled in - an invented threshold turns an unchecked path into an apparently checked one.

enable_tiers.description: Rails grouped into the tiers the enable graph FORCES. Rails inside one tier come up together: the graph does not order them, and claiming it does would invent a sequence the hardware never promised. A cycle is refused outright, because a topological sort that drops the cycle's members reports a shorter and entirely plausible order.

declared_order.description: The written power-up order, compared against the enable graph. Only an INVERSION counts as a contradiction: a document ordering two rails the graph leaves in one tier is stating an intent the hardware permits, not contradicting it.

margin_v.description: Source rail minus threshold. The sign decides whether the regulator turns on at all; the size decides whether it still does over temperature and tolerance, which is why a thin positive margin is a separate finding from a negative one.

budget_v.description: null means the total was computed but nothing called it acceptable, because nothing said what acceptable was.

rule.description: Deterministic contributors are correlated and add linearly; random ones add in quadrature. Summing a deterministic term in quadrature UNDERSTATES it, which is the direction that ships, so a contributor's kind is not cosmetic.
